key_insight: This paper gives the first complete fixed-domain asymptotic theory for joint MLE of Gaussian process RBF kernel parameters—spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget—showing consistency, optimal rates, and asymptotic normality.
engineering_relevance: It provides theoretical justification for how GP hyperparameters are estimated in real software, improving confidence in kernel fitting for scientific computing, spatial modeling, and Bayesian optimization.
method: Analyze joint maximum likelihood estimation under fixed-domain asymptotics for the RBF kernel.
Prove consistency, derive convergence rates, and establish joint asymptotic normality for all three parameters.
Show the rates are minimax optimal.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a full asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE, including consistency, rates, and asymptotic normality, rather than a purely empirical evaluation.
watch_item: The results are asymptotic and fixed-domain specific, so practical performance may differ for finite samples or under increasing-domain settings.
paper_title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
